28.text: COMPARATIVE NOTES. — Judging from my own information and that

29.text: collected by Mr. Jochelson, the religious ideas of the Koryak present many

30.text: close similarities to those of the Chukchee, not only in their general character,

31.text: but also in their way of development. Thus, Mr. Jochelson says that

32.text: “household utensils, implements, parts of the house, the chamber-vessel, and

33.text: even excrement, have an existence of their own. They may warn their

34.text: ‘masters’ of danger, and attack their enemies.”¹ This corresponds to what
